title: Efficient Simple Temporal Cycle Enumeration on Large Graphs with Lightweight Preprocessing

problem.claim: Enumerate all simple cycles with strictly increasing timestamps within a given time window.

gap.claim: Existing methods suffer from redundant checks and an expensive detection phase, limiting efficiency on large-scale or dynamically evolving graphs.

contributions.claim: An edge-centric framework treats temporal edges as the core units of exploration.
The framework computes edge offsets in linear time and uses constraint-based DFS to avoid redundant temporal checks and the expensive detection phase.
An incremental update algorithm selectively identifies affected paths for dynamic settings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce a novel edge-centric framework for simple temporal cycle enumeration.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The design provides polynomial delay and substantial performance gains over existing approaches.
Experiments report over an order-of-magnitude speedup on static graphs and up to six orders-of-magnitude improvement for dynamic updates.
Most dynamic updates reportedly complete within 1 ms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal cycles are presented as important graph patterns with applications in finance, security, and neuroscience.
The work studies enumeration of simple temporal cycles with strictly increasing timestamps within a time window.
Prior methods are described as inefficient because of redundant checks and an expensive detection phase.
The proposed framework uses edge-centric exploration, linear-time edge offsets, constraint-based DFS, and incremental dynamic updates.
The authors report polynomial delay, large speedups, and sub-millisecond completion for most updates.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines beyond 2SCENT, hardware, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide formal complexity details beyond polynomial delay.
The abstract does not describe the dynamic update model or correctness validation.
